original_question: Let G be a hyperbolic group. Does there exist a number p in [2, infinity) and an l_p complex on which G acts geometrically such that either (i) the complex has a convex bicombing, or (ii) the complex is Busemann convex?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Question 7.1, "ℓ^p models for hyperbolic groups." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper's question: the ambient class is hyperbolic groups, the unknown is the existence of some ℓ^p complex, the action is required to be geometric, and the two geometric conditions named in the paper are exactly "has a convex bicombing" and "is Busemann convex." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
missing_details: The paper does not restrict to p ≥ 2. In the surrounding motivation, the point is to ask for some finite p, i.e. an "ℓ^p-type" model with p < ∞, so the lower bound 2 in the draft is stronger than the paper and should be removed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

Immediately before Question 7.1, the paper defines an ℓ^p complex as a simplicial complex metrized so that each cell is isometric to a simplex of ℓ^p. That definition is needed if the question is to stand alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

To make the rewrite self-contained, the standard phrase "acts geometrically" should be expanded as acting properly and cocompactly by isometries; the paper itself uses the standard shorthand. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

The nearby context defines a bicombing as a chosen geodesic c_xy between each pair x,y, and calls it convex when t ↦ d(c_xy(t), c_x'y'(t)) is convex for all x,y,x',y'. That definition is implicit in the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

The paper explains that Busemann convexity is the stronger bicombing-type condition: the space is uniquely geodesic and its unique bicombing is convex. The draft names Busemann convexity but does not unpack it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

In the paper, the convex-bicombing and Busemann-convex versions are best read as two nested versions of the same problem, with the Busemann-convex version stronger. Writing them only as an undifferentiated either/or loses that structure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

There are no ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions here; the hidden assumptions are purely metric-geometric and come from the definitions supplied in Section 7. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
refined_question: For every hyperbolic group G, does there exist some finite p and an ℓ^p complex X—meaning a simplicial complex metrized so that each cell is isometric to a simplex of ℓ^p—on which G acts geometrically, such that X admits a convex geodesic bicombing (i.e. a choice of geodesic c_xy joining each pair x,y ∈ X for which t ↦ d(c_xy(t), c_x'y'(t)) is convex for all x,y,x',y' ∈ X)? More strongly, can X be chosen Busemann convex, equivalently uniquely geodesic with its unique bicombing convex? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 7, Question 7.1: the official statement uses the same four ingredients almost verbatim—hyperbolic group, existence of an ℓ^p complex, geometric action, and the two properties "convex bicombing" / "Busemann convex." The surrounding Section 7 discussion supplies the missing paper-faithful scope: it motivates the problem as a weakening of the CAT(0) question for hyperbolic groups, recalls Lang's injective ℓ^∞ model, then asks for a finite-p analogue; it also defines convex bicombings, explains that Busemann convexity is the stronger condition, and defines an ℓ^p complex immediately before Question 7.1. So the main fixes are to remove the unnecessary bound p ∈ [2,∞), add the paper's definition of ℓ^p complex, and phrase the Busemann-convex version as the stronger refinement of the convex-bicombing version rather than as a loose alternative. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))
